tips.comment: Eternal Sunshine was a close third at Musselburgh last time and returns to a track she loves. Dropping to Class 5 with Mulrennan back on, she looks set for a big run.

LE BEAU GARCON makes his seasonal reappearance and he has worthwhile form when fresh. He is a multiple sprint winner on quick ground , so with conditions possibly more in his favour than any others he could be one the stable are relying on today.
Back to his best last time and a massive chance here from a mark 3lb lower than from what he won off a year ago.
Sea Legend wasn’t far away at Newcastle last time and is back on turf off a mark 3lb below his last win. With Mulrennan booked, he’s got a decent chance.

The appearance was against some decent horses and ran well, only coming a length behind. It is a course and distance winner and is reunited with Connor BEasley today. With some extra fitness now, it can go very close.
Ten wins around at this course and he still looks to be on a good mark even after being raised 4lbs. He has a good central draw and should go well today.

Crimson Road has been a bit down the pack since changing yards in March but did last win on GF running off an 80. He showed improvement when last out when returning to C4 and might be ready off today's 75.

Sophiesticate is my long shot for today. She last won in June last year off a 68 but interestingly was second here in August off a 68 as well. She is now second up after a long break and a duff return and will be all the better for that run so could be a surprise now second up off a 61 with Amie claiming 3 lbs EW.
The well-bred 2yo colt is making his debut in this maiden race. He cost £200K at the breeze-up sales. Top yard/jockey and should give a good account of himself.

One of the interesting runners who improved on the second outing at Beverly. Upped in trip for the first time today after the two runs, and Beasley is on board for the first time, replacing B. Robinson.

A Cotai Glory Colt, a half-brother to multiple winners, including the impressive Champers Elysees, who has triumphed at distances up to 1 mile, and the capable Daddies Girl, who has won at 8.3 furlongs. His dam, although a maiden, has shown potential by staying 1 and a quarter miles. Kieran O'Neill, known for his strong performances at Ayr with 3 victories and 6 placements from 13 races in the past 5 years, will be in the saddle. At 18/1, this colt presents excellent value, especially as a solid each-way bet for this promising 2-year-old.

Well bred 2 year old filly trained by Jim Goldie who has a great record at Ayr and it's interesting that he introduces Saxon Gem in a race like this. The price is way too big and could produce a shock.

Regular readers will know that I simply don't back Luke Morris (unless the horse has 10lb+ in hand perhaps!). So whenever he is replaced by a better jockey, I like to have a deeper delve. James Doyle takes over now, and the cheekpieces go on too after that slightly disappointing 3rd last time out. He races off the same mark here, and I suspect this jockey will hold the horse up and come with a late run. I'm prepared to take the 2/1 that he'll give the horse a much better ride than the horse was given last time out.

The 5yo is a previous C/D winner. Two runs this year, making a forward move three weeks ago on the AW but was hampered at a vital stage. He’ll enjoy the return to this fast turf ground. Weighted to run a big race. Three of the main rivals in this 6-runner handicap like to go hard at the front end, which could set it up nicely for the selection who likes to come from off the pace.

Woohoo won for the first time at the 10th attempt at Hamilton last Friday over 5 furlongs. That was an apprentice handicap, so she has no penalty. If as effective at 6 furlongs, she looks likely to go in again.

Lightly raced 4yo. Respectable run two weeks ago, only 7th of 13 but only beaten 2L and he didn’t have a good track position, but saw the race out nicely from off the pace. He was given an 80 rating after winning last spring and is now down to a mark of 60 after being dropped another 2lb after that last run. The six runners that beat him in that last race were rated 72-77. His highest rated rival in this handicap has a mark of 58.

Winner at Thirsk in October. Mostly solid efforts on the all-weather since and ran well when 4th back on turf at Leicester last month. Dropped a lb for that, so should be firmly in the mix this afternoon.
Not ready to give up on her, especially now with a dropped mark and a 3lb claimer. She was off for 4 months before the LTO effort at Hamilton this month, so expecting a more competitive run today.

Heritor is a 4-year-old gelding trained by R Mike Smith. He makes his handicap debut today off 54 and has finished 9-7-7, posting a career-high RPR of 56. He should probably be avoided like the plague, particularly as jockey Rhys Elliott is 0-20 wins at Ayr for R Mike Smith and has been sent off at 200-1 in all three starts. However, there are some positives as Heritor did show some promise on his last start over CD. Secondly, he is one of four foals, incidentally all trained by R Mike Smith, and Earn Your Stripes won twice off 46-50 at Hamilton and Ayr over today's trip. So, R Mike Smith knows this family well. R Mike Smith also targets this meeting, picking up 52 winners, more winners than at any other track in the country. It's a speculative bet, but it's a low-grade class 6 handicap and could surprise off 49 with Rhys Elliott's 5lb apprentice claim.

Mark Walford has his string going very nicely just now, and he has found a fantastic opportunity for Beltane to get his first win in many a long day. Most of these are very ordinary sorts that won't take much beating. Beltane, despite not winning for ages, has been running quite well lately, and does try, which makes him an attractive bet in this race.

Has won from off the pace last June (1m3f) off 2lb lower. A modest 3rd on penultimate run and unraced on this short of trip. Good each-way chance. Beltane looks the one to beat. But if the first time cheekpieces have an adverse affect then she's (penelopes sister) in with a good chance.

The 4-year-old filly enjoyed the return to turf and a shorter trip three weeks ago. She was 3rd over 8.5f, beaten around 2L behind a progressive winner, seeing the race out nicely. It was her first run on quick ground turf and something to build on. Chances over this 8f off her low mark, in this class 6 handicap.

Little Empire heads to Ayr today after a solid fourth at Dundalk over a mile in March, beaten just over a length. He’s back at a track where he’s won before and has Danny Tudhope booked, so if he’s ready to fire off the break, he could be in the mix.

The 4yo has 2 wins from 9 on turf and only one poor run in defeat. He can return stronger after 7 months off the track and he had a wind op during the spring. He won his final start last year - only 2lb higher now. His two races prior to that win he went close twice over this 7f C/D. The jockey booking does suggest he’ll be in decent shape for his return.

Sir Garfield has demonstrated a strong affinity for Ayr, securing a victory over this course and distance on October 1, 2024, in a Class 6 handicap. His consistent form at this venue includes multiple runner-up finishes, indicating he's well-suited to the track. 
His recent form includes a sixth-place finish at Doncaster over 6f2y on May 3, 2025, where he was beaten by just over six lengths on good to firm ground. This performance suggests he's holding his form and capable of making an impact in this field. 
With the going at Ayr expected to be good to firm, conditions should suit Sir Garfield well. His proven ability over the distance and experience at the course make him an appealing each-way proposition at likely generous odds.

Inanna has won 4 of her 29 starts and is very consistent, having also been placed on 9 occasions. She won over course and distance earlier this month, and she is just 2 lbs higher. The stable is in excellent form with 6 winners in the past week, and this one looks a good each way with 4 places on offer.
Moyola has not been great of late but did win last June off a 69. It comes into today after a short break and wind surgery, running off a 64 with Warren in the saddle claiming 5 lbs EW 4P.

Only 2-32 but a fairly consistent performer who should come on for reappearance 5th at Doncaster last month. Not one for maximum faith given his record but has won off higher previously, so unlikely to be far away.

Rory was going well in May last year. Wearing cheekpieces, he finished a close second over today's course and distance. That headgear, in which he has previously won, is back on today for the first time in 21 outings. Rory has won at Ayr. He has scored over today's distance. His turf successes have been on a sound surface. Rory has dropped in the weights and has been given a chance by the handicapper.

This one is the rank outsider of the field, but could well be the surprise package. He's drawn 11 of 14, which is a positive, and he gets in here off 65 on handicap debut with the jockey who is having a breakthrough season, taking 3lb off. If you take a close look at the horse's 4th of 8 at a huge price on the AW last time out, you'll see that the horse could certainly have finished a lot closer, but there was an element of protecting his future handicap mark. Despite that, there are still clues to unravel, such as he finished just ahead of El Pinto, who he gave 7lbs to, and that horse had previously been sandwiched between 80(ish) rated horses when 2nd. So this provides further clues that Dwindling Funds might be no forlorn hope here off 65.

Connie's Rose returns to action in the 15:55 Dragonbet Born From The Betting Ring Handicap (Class 4) at Chepstow, a 5f16y contest on good to firm ground. Trained by Grace Harris, this 6-year-old bay mare by Adaay carries a rating of 68 into this 6-runner field. 
Notably, Connie's Rose has demonstrated a strong affinity for Chepstow, securing multiple victories over this course and distance. Her recent form includes a commendable third-place finish at Chepstow over 6f16y on May 13, 2025, where she was narrowly beaten by a head in a Class 5 handicap, indicating she's holding her form well. 
With the going at Chepstow expected to be good to firm, conditions should suit Connie's Rose, who has proven her adaptability across different ground types.

This unexposed horse can capitalize on the favorite having to defy a penalty after winning last time out. Step Along made her turf debut last time out when 9th of 15 after 6 months off. More importantly, the 4th of 9 in an all-weather novice race last year, she was in and around horses raced around 10lb and more than the mark she races off here today. Now that she is fit after that run last time out, I think this well-bred horse is clearly on a winnable mark.

Bottom of the handicap mark and thrice-raced maiden, and performances not given much confidence to the market. However, 2 of these 3 runs have been here over C&D and now going down in class, so anything is possible.
Won with plenty in hand, and because that was an apprentice's race, comes into this from the same mark, making this one a very strong bet.
The A Wintle yard recently burst into super form, and the best looking of the three running today looks like CD winner Soi Dao under Taryn Langley claiming 7lb. EW player at least.
Makes course debut tomorrow. Current form is nothing to get excited about, but hoping he can get back to the good form at Ascot last September, which was off a much higher mark.

Vape heads to Chepstow today after a decent fourth at Wolverhampton last time. He’s got Oisin Murphy booked and is drawn in stall 5, which should give him options. If he builds on that last run, he’s got a fair shout in this Class 6 sprint.

Regulars will know I love a weak race where I can seemingly discount a few at shorter prices, and I think that's the case with DIAMOND COTTAGE here. Disappointed over this trip last time out, but that was in a big field, and this is a drop in distance which should help. Handicap mark still looks workable, and the draw doesn't look too bad either. Neither was the run before last at Salisbury.

Richard Hannon saddles the first and second favorite here, and I like the look of Emma Rebecca, who was raced over an inadequate 7f while gaining a handicap qualifying mark. Since getting her mark, she has raced over 1m2f twice, finishing second both times. The extra 2 furlongs today are very likely a big positive, and an improved run is very much on the cards.

Crackamour makes his turf debut in a very low class 6. The horse, I admit, has done little or nothing of note to date, but I am very taken by the breeding. Although it ran poorly at Wolverhampton over the distance at the end of April, I am certain turf will bring about an improvement.
Eye-catching run when finishing strongly in a hot race at Chester last time. Managed that from a wide draw and won't face any similar disadvantage here.
Both trainers' 2-year-old runners this year have won, and this one received a positive mention at the weekend and should be ready.

Well-bred colt by No Nay Never and related to multiple winners including He's A Monster and Festive Fare; represents top connections with Oisin Murphy booked and trainer A M Balding in form. Pedigree suggests early speed, and this looks a good starting point. Big player on debut.

Had a difficult debut when 13 of 13 at Leicester earlier this month but I think he still warrants appeal given the huge price and also the sire (Sands of Mali (FR)) who is profitable in the last 22 days and has a useful strike rate of 14.4% which is better than the average.

Triple Gee's debut was a fair 3rd at Salisbury and was not fully asked for more effort that day. Showed plenty of promise, especially considering it was his first run and given it was on firm ground at Salisbury. There’s every reason to expect improvement with good ground expected today. Bred to stay well and may take a step forward here. May still be learning but has definite win potential if building on debut effort.

Sits on a lovely looking mark at present, 15 lbs below his opening handicap mark. Admittedly, he does seem to be regressing, but I'm not convinced he was ever a chaser. The fact he won 2 of his 7 runs over hurdles and no wins from 5 runs over fences would support that theory. He finished 2nd in a Grade 2 over hurdles, bumping into the useful Fennors Cross, beaten just over 3L by the winner. He also finished a fair 3rd in the Dovecote Grade 2 novices behind Rubuad in his pomp. He showed nothing over fences last term. He reverted to hurdles off the back of a long break just over 3 weeks ago. He ran well, to be fair, beaten just 7L behind Glory And Fortune, back in 3rd place. He's been dropped a handy 3 lbs for that effort. He should strip fitter for that pipe opener last time out.

The model I run suggests Time Interval should win this race. This result has largely been driven by Time Interval having a relatively high RPR compared to the 8 runners in this field. Has a kind official ranking, leaving Time Interval carrying relatively low weight compared to its peers. This horse is one of only two who have placed recently (won 13 days ago this distance). The model has issued a low confidence reading, indicating only a 0.5pts bet (on a scale of 0-4).

Five starts over hurdles for the 5yo, form 31120. Something amiss when last seen but has since had a 2 month break to freshen up. A good runner-up on his handicap debut during March. The drop down to this 2m trip on quick ground looks very positive going off his wide margin maiden win last Oct. This front runner might be hard to catch.

Sean Bowen's only ride in this meeting piques my interest here. Only one booking for the day? There must be a huge chance that the market thinks he can win. With other horses in this race that have achieved much more, what makes this one special? Is he today's dark horse? The market seems to think so.

The model I run suggests Rukaana should win this race. This model result has been driven by Rukaana having the joint highest RPR of this 8-runner field. It has a middle-order official ranking, meaning the mark should be reasonable relative to RPR. Rukaana subsequently carries a middle-order amount of weights compared to the other runners. Rukaana ran a good second 12 days ago and looks to go one better here in good form. The model predicts this race to be very tight and therefore only issued a low confidence reading. For that reason, 0.5 pts bet on a scale of 0-4.

Cusano took a big step forward when second in a C4 on returning from a break after wind surgery. Although 10L away from the winner, he was hampered by a faller at the last. I expect more today while dropping in grade to C5.

Sits just 1lb above his last winning mark. Coming into this off the back of a very good effort last time out. 
He's 3 from 3 at this venue. 2 from 2 over course and distance. This is clearly a course that suits him very well. 
His most recent win rates decent form. He beat Irish Hill quite comfortably at Wincanton off a 1lb lower mark. That horse is rated 133, and actually won off a mark of 131 just 3 months ago. Clearly, he's beaten a decent horse. 
He's shown very little since then. That was until he ran at Newton Abbot just 7 days ago. With the first-time blinkers on, he ran a cracker behind the in-form American Land. Beaten just over 2 lengths by the winner, back in 3rd place. 
The blinkers are left on again this time. If they work again, with the return to his favorite course being a plus, I think he can go well off this type of mark.

The model I run suggests Honneur D'Ajonc can win this race. Honneur D'Ajonc lines up with the second highest RPR of the 7-runner field. It has an assigned official ranking near middle order, and that leaves a reasonable weight being carried over this 2m 5f. Alex Chadwick on board relieves a further 5 lbs, taking the total weight carried down towards the lower order of the 7 runners. It is the only horse in this field who has shown recent signs of form apart from Crystal Glance, placing and coming 2nd 15 days ago. There are a couple of runners here who have not raced in a long time. The model has issued a moderate confidence reading. 1.0 pt bet on a 0-4 scale.

A mark of 108 looks rather eye-catching for one that has previously been as high as 116. Fell two out when last seen 43 days ago, holding every chance at the time. That was over a slightly shorter trip than today's, with the step back up here being in favor.

The 6yo has a progressive-looking profile, with 3 wins over hurdles. A big run two starts back, 2nd of 9, beaten just 2L, and the front three had pulled 13L clear of the rest in a good quality 0-140 rated handicap. The highest rival in this race is 115. The winner from that race has boosted the form since and is rated 15lb higher now. It was his first run over this 21f trip, and he has similar good ground again. Excuses last time out - heavy ground. Comes here fresh after a 4-month break.

Roadshow returned from a break in March, running for a new yard and having had wind surgery. He was a decent second when last out two weeks ago, when stepping up to 2m1f with more expected at today's trip.

Two starts over hurdles for the 5-year-old. He was 3rd of 10 during March. Only 6th of 7 five weeks ago, but it was a very strong novice hurdle. He jumped fine and stayed in touch for a good way. Similar trip for this maiden hurdle. He can take a step forward, and this race is not nearly as strong as his last race.

Pride Of Paris was having only his second start over fences when beaten just a neck on debut at Uttoxeter earlier this month. The extra 1.5f today should help, and up just 2lbs, he looks the most likely winner here.

The 6yo lost his form over the winter but was back on his game four weeks ago, when beaten just a length. Suited by the 3m trip on decent ground. He went very close last Oct while racing off a 7lb higher mark. Still room for improvement over fences.

The model I run suggests an upset can be caused by McGregors Charge. McGregors Charge lines up with the second highest RPR of this smaller 6 runner field. Subsequently, it goes out carrying the least amount of weight around this longer 3m 1f trip. There is a minimum weight differential of a full stone here to the current market leaders (and even more for some other runners). That kind of weight difference over this distance should be telling by the end. The model suggests this is a good value bet, but only a slightly higher % chance of McGregors Charge winning than some of the other runners. Therefore, it has issued a low stake reading (0.75pts bet on a scale of 0-4).

Lightly raced 7yo, good yard/jockey. Yet to win over fences in five starts but his two runs when stepping up to this 20f trip and racing on good ground have resulted in two 1L defeats. He can build on his narrow defeat from four weeks ago and there are question marks against his four rivals.

First time over the fences. Won a 20 furlong hurdle event in fine style in a very quick timed event, with trainer Skelton showing a 35% win rate at this course and chase events, and jockey Skelton showing a 29% win rate at this course and chase events. 4/1 has invited me in for an each way play.

The model I run suggests Cat Tiger can win this one. Cat Tiger is a veteran at this age but lines up here with the highest RPR of all the runners. It has an official ranking very close to the other runners, where all the weight differences are minimal. Cat Tiger placed well 35 days ago and looks to build on that here over this similar 2m 4f trip. The model has issued a very low confidence reading for this, taking into account the probability of winning, value compared to the current price, and gap to the horse in second in the simulation. 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Brize Norton returns to Kempton today after a solid third at Salisbury last October. He’s drawn in stall 1 and has Hector Crouch back on board, which should help him get a good early position. If he’s come on over the winter, he’s got a decent shot in this novice.

A Circus Maximus gelding with strong connections to 3 winners, such as the talented New York Girl, who has excelled at 9f, and the solid 7f performer Broadway Duchess. The 20/1 odds are attractive, particularly given de Foy's current 14% strike rate, making an each-way bet look very promising with de la Sayette on board.

Cosi Bello looks the one here after a smart win at Chelmsford. The form of that race was worked out well, with both the second and the third running big races since. Drawn well and open to plenty of improvement, he's got a strong chance of following up and keeping his unbeaten record.

Steady progress is being made with this one. It has improved with each of its 3 outings so far and was a close 3rd latest. Looks at much better value than the front 2 in the betting and a sound each-way chance.

This yard isn't particularly well known for its winners on the flat, but I always follow Territories as a sire in sprint events. Pam Sly has a 25% strike rate with her 3-year-olds, and I'm hoping that WRYDCROFT might sneak a place in this. Grey's Monument was a 116-rated horse, and he too was by Territories out of a mare whose sire was Teofilo. If this horse was anywhere near as good as that, he could well show very well in this contest.

Frostmagic comes into this off a career-best win at Doncaster over 1m2f, where he made all and held on gamely. He’s up 6lb for that but still looks well-treated off 62. Back down to a mile, he’s got a solid shot at following up if he gets the lead again.

To me, this looks like the obvious bet going on its previous form at this track. It is the only C/D winner in the field and has always run better on the Polytrack. Top jockey booked and at generous odds with 4 places available, looks like a no-brainer punt.

Letsbeatsepsis steps up to a mile at Kempton after two unplaced runs in Class 4 company over shorter trips. He’s now down to a mark of 63 and drops into Class 6, which should make things easier. He’s shown a bit of promise in the past, placing twice as a 2yo, and this looks like a more realistic spot to get involved.

Al Ameen has demonstrated a strong affinity for Kempton, securing back-to-back victories over this course and distance in March and April 2025. His recent form includes a commendable fifth-place finish at Kempton over 6 furlongs on April 15, 2025, where he was beaten by just over three lengths in a Class 4 handicap, indicating he's holding his form well. 
With the Polytrack surface at Kempton expected to suit him, and considering his proven ability over the distance, Al Ameen presents as an appealing each-way proposition at likely generous odds.
Class Angle and significant jockey booking, I think, is prime for a big run here. Course Specialist doesn't run a bad race.

Winner over C&D, albeit a few years ago. Perhaps more relevant, unlucky not to win a class 2 race here in February and then got a second place in a class 4. Good jockey on board and back at a good mark.

Poor form continues even for new yard when 15 of 15 LTO at Doncaster back in March of this year. But hoping this horse has been training well since and is now operating only 1lb higher than the last winning mark. Makes course debut today.

Al Barez heads back to Kempton tonight after a solid second at Wolverhampton last month, where he was just half a length behind the winner. He’s only been nudged up 1lb for that run and returns to a track where he’s already won twice over 6f. With a favourable draw, he’s got a strong chance of going one better.

Windsor novice winner in the summer of 23 who has clearly had his problems since but has run well a couple of times at Southwell so far this spring. Still retains plenty of potential so should run well this evening.

Brunel Charm returns to action in the 20:10 Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap (Class 4) at Kempton, a 6f contest on Polytrack. Trained by Charlie Wallis, this 8-year-old bay gelding by Charm Spirit carries a rating of 72 into this race tomorrow.
Notably, Brunel Charm has demonstrated a strong affinity for Kempton, securing a victory over this course and distance on January 20, 2025, in a Class 6 handicap. His recent form includes a win at Chelmsford on March 13, 2025, and a commendable third-place finish at Chelmsford on February 22, 2025, indicating he's holding his form well. 
With the Polytrack surface at Kempton expected to suit him, and considering his proven ability over the distance, Brunel Charm presents as an appealing each-way proposition at likely generous odds.

Starfighter lines up at Kempton tonight after a string of consistent efforts over similar trips. He was a close third here in March and has been holding his form well since. Back on the all-weather and off a workable mark, he’s got a decent shot if things fall his way.

The mount of S De Sousa is always worth taking a look at. Good Eye started its career making its best in distances similar to today's but later failed racing in a mile or less. Despite severe opposition, it can be expected to be driven to win or be close with the booking of so excellent jockey.

Understandable rustiness when only 7 of 7 at Wolverhampton back in March of this year, but that was the first run since May of 2023. However, form did not change LTO when 11 of 12 here over C&D. Now back down to last winning mark, and a drop down in class should help.

Extrication showed promise on his seasonal return over 7f at Kempton, finishing strongly from the rear to be nearest at the finish. Stepping back up to a mile should suit, and he’s on a mark that gives him a decent chance to get involved.

CITY OF YORK is a C&D winner who has steadily dropped 11lb down the weights during the past 13 months and is now 3lb below his last winning mark. He is well-drawn in stall 1 and if a recent pipe-opener at Chelmsford in a much more valuable higher Class race than this, has blew away the cobwebs he is weighted to go close in this. Please see my X feed for a more detailed write-up.

Decent 0-75 Class 5 handicap over 1 mile. One of two runners here for Ian Williams, both low in the handicap. Law Supreme gets the vote, looking a value pick at 12-1. Cieren Fallon is booked. The stable has come into form recently. Law Supreme ran well when fourth of ten over course and distance two weeks ago. That was the six-year-old's first start for five months and could come on for the outing yet. Handicap mark has dropped from 83 when joining the yard to a low of 66 here. Two wins and seven places from 25 runs under rules. Good claims from this handicap mark.

Arctician stepped up in grade last time out and was drawn in the car park, so I think we can readily draw a line through that. Was second the run before here, from the same stall, and now returns to this trip with a more favourable draw and a reduced mark to boot. Jock got him home from a pound higher in the weights at the beginning of the year, and I think this trip is potentially within his remit.

Pop Dancer heads to Brighton today after a front-running win at Goodwood earlier this month. He’s up 3lb but has a great draw in stall 1 and has won twice over this course and distance before. If he gets out in front again, he could be hard to peg back.

Immediate Effect returns to action at Brighton after a solid debut win at Wolverhampton and a close second at Southwell last autumn. He’s stepping up to a mile for the first time, which should suit his running style. With Luke Morris booked and a good draw, he’s got a strong chance of making a successful seasonal reappearance.

Fav matches the time at Southwell, when finishing a creditable 2nd. At 9/2, each way play for Duca looks a good bet. Was far from disgraced when finishing 8th from 9 runners in a competitive class 3 event. Top jockey on board here, fares well at this course. Class 5 event, in a small field, definitely see place.

Poetic Force lines up at Brighton today, a track where he’s enjoyed multiple wins over the years. He was a close third here last month and remains on a workable mark of 55. With Jack Doughty back on board and a decent draw, he’s got a fair shot if the race unfolds to suit.

Local Bay returns to Brighton today after a strong second over a mile here three weeks ago, where he only gave way late on. Now back to 7f off the same mark, and with Jack Doughty riding again, he looks well set to go one better if he gets a clear run.

Starsong showed improvement after a short break in April when not far away in third in a C6, followed by a similar run to second a couple of weeks ago in C5. I think the return to C6, just 1 lb heavier today and having Luke Morris to help out, could see yet more improvement.

The last time this horse had a fast ground 7 furlongs race resulted in a 2nd place finish where the third came out and won their next race. That was off 69 and she's down to just 64 now. The horses regular jockey doesn't have stats anywhere near as good as Harry Davies so the jockey switch is seen as a major positive for me. The horse also won her only other race in this class and despite the weakness in the early market, she looks to have a serious chance and the 12/1 looks generous.

Latona has not been far away for all three runs this year, with the latest last month only missing out by 2L with no extra on the run-in. Which makes me think she is worth a chance now dropping to 7f.

Rock Master ran a decent race at Chelmsford last time, doing plenty up front before just getting caught late. Back on turf now and returns to Brighton where conditions should suit. With Tom Marquand booked and a handy draw, he’s got a shot if he sees it out better this time.

Inventress made a promising debut at Cork earlier this month when second over 1m 2.5f. She should be suited by the drop back to 8 furlongs, and with the stable having 3 winners at Cork yesterday, she looks the most likely winner here.

Pierre Royal is a 3-year-old son of Kingman ex Rose Pierre, whose dam is Profound Beauty by Danehill. He was unraced as a 2-year-old. Last time out on his racecourse debut, he was 4 lengths second at 9/4 behind First Wave 9/4 by Wootton Bassett over this course and distance earlier this month. He'll be ridden by C Hayes for DK Weld & the Moyglare Stud. He's drawn 1/8, and if he jumps and gets the rail position, he should oblige for his owner/breeder. The stable has a good record in maidens at this track. Maybe one for your horse tracker.

Comfort Line is a 9-time winner overall, and recent form has been good with 1 win and a couple of runner-up finishes inside the last handful of outings. Course and distance winner here too, and definitely looks the one to beat.

MOTHER MARA is an interesting three year old filly who looks better than her mark in this Claiming race. Syndicate owned now and formerly trained in Britain it is hard to know if today is the day she will be seen to good effect , but the market will likely reveal more.

A lightly-raced maiden worth attention. Recently, she finished 9th in a claimer at this course 35 days ago and is now racing for a new yard after leaving Prendergast. With A J Casey riding well and providing a 10lb claim, this filly could be a smart each-way bet at 20/1, promising a good chance of a profit.

At a price, I'll try the long-time loser here, Feature This, blinkered for the first time off a lowly mark, now dropping into a claimer under a 10 lb claimer. Who has yet to win? Lots to like after it showed up for a good way last time.

Skontonovski has won 11 times, with his last win on turf coming at Thurles off a mark of 52 last October. He moved to Gerard O'Leary's yard earlier this year and has disappointed in his 3 starts for them. Although only 12th at Curragh earlier this month, he was only beaten 7 lengths and dropped 5 lbs. Looks like a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.

ASISAID was a well punted runner in a competitive enough handicap latest. That market confidence likely signals the yard have come into good form and potentially now having come back to hand well treated this one appeals as a likely each-way type.

I'm not usually one to go back in on a horse after it's been hit with a few extra pounds - the value often disappears second time around - but at current odds of 20/1, I'm more than happy to side with Paul Fahey’s 5-year-old gelding GIANH RIVER.
He left all previous form behind when finishing a career-best 2nd here at Gowran Park, over this very trip and on good ground. That effort looks even stronger when you factor in that jockey Jessica Gorman reported the saddle slipped in the dying strides, which likely explains why he was hanging slightly left late on.
This son of TONKIN has been raised 4lbs for that run, which seems fair enough. Gorman keeps the ride and crucially claims a very handy 7lbs again.
Plenty to like here at the price - and with a smoother round, he could go one better. I’m happy to have a punt and find out.

FAMOUS ENOUGH is still only a five year old so he should have more to offer. He has the hood retained following a promising effort latest and there is a chance he could step forward on the back of that run. His lowly near-basement rating tempers enthusiasm a little , but he does appear overpriced.

Sioux Eagle has a wide draw to overcome, but don't let that put you off here. Now a pound lower, Sioux Eagle, with his form being very consistent and a great 4th place last time out here days ago, can easily stay this 1m 6f and is very consistent with placing at this trip. I do believe that now he is looking like a win is due.

DISCO BOY should appreciate this distance and his recent handicap debut was promising. That effort showed him a capable sort from this mark and he can be expected to progress third-up from a break here. A lightly-raced six year old who looks to have sound claims.

Chris Hayes rode a winner on the Flat on last ride for Gordon Elliott (SR 15%). Miss Gitana looks a decent price at 7-1 or bigger. Four year-old filly by Nathaniel (good staying pedigree) who put together a solid string of decent results, winning twice at this trip on good-firm ground for Mark Prescott last year. Has been running in maiden hurdles for this yard and put in a better effort than 28-1 might have suggested in a decent handicap over 1m5f at Navan on only Flat outing for this yard so far. Was making up ground late and should be better for slightly longer trip and firmer going here. Chance.

This year the 8-year-old has secured 1 win from 3 outings, with her most recent success at Dundalk in March. She also delivered a solid performance, finishing 3rd of 8 in a 12f handicap at Dundalk 47 days ago. Definitely a contender, and with the jockey's 10lb claim, the 20/1 odds present a tempting opportunity for an each-way bet.

This Pinatubo filly is a promising prospect, being a half-sister to the 1m winner Suwayra and the accomplished 1 and a quarter to 1 and half mile winner Sumiha. Her Dam, a 1 and quarter mile winner, is also half-sister to the exceptional Sinawann, who excelled up to 1m and stayed 1 and a quarter mile. With the Weld yard performing exceptionally well and a skilled jockey on board, the 20/1 odds present an excellent opportunity for an each-way wager.

Fine Print won twice on the AW at Wolverhampton in April and returned to turf with a good second at Navan on Saturday. He is 7 lbs better off with the winner for a 2 lengths defeat, so looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

DUKE OTTO is looking well treated as an in-form runner and he should be capable of transferring his form back to racing on the level from his attractive looking mark under this code. He is turned around quickly which reads well possibly with connections spying this opportunity and he rates a strong contender.

I’d give RED SECRET a small squeak here. Kevin Smith's charge met trouble LTO in Navan, supported from 12/1 - 17/2 and chance gone thereafter. He’s won twice on the all-weather but has a few bits of place form in good ground from last season. Wesley Joyce rode a winner for Smith last week and teams up again. This mark isn’t too taxing, I’d hope, as he finished 3rd three times last year off this number. There’s plenty in this with better form albeit shorter odds. Chancing a tentative ew.
